title: Universal Hand-held Three-dimensional Optoacoustic Imaging Probe for Deep Tissue Human Angiography and Functional Preclinical Studies in Real Time
protocol: Switch on the laser for a warm-up period of ~15 min prior to operation.
Place the water enclosing part with the isolating membrane that is in contact with the skin.
Fill the whole volume between the isolating membrane and the surface of the transducer with deionized water by means of a pump.
Ensure no water leakage or air bubbles are present in the water.
Apply ultrasound gel onto the skin around the region to be imaged.
Place the optoacoustic probe in the region of interest.
Ensure no air bubbles are present in the ultrasound coupling gel.
Ensure that the care and experimental procedures with animals are in agreement with institutional and government rules and regulations.
Remove the fur of the animal in the region to be imaged with a shaving lotion.
Protect the eyes of the animal with vet ointment.

Anesthetize the animal by using intraperitoneal injection (IP) of ketamine/xylazine (100 mg/kg KG Ketamine + 5 mg/kg KG Xylazine) prior to the experiment or use isoflurane anesthesia (2-3 % (by volume) with 0.9 l/min gas flow) during the experiment.
Confirm anesthetization by checking the reflex of the hind limb of the animal.
Apply ultrasound gel onto the skin around the region to be imaged in order to provide efficient acoustic coupling.
Place the optoacoustic probe in the region of interest.
Ensure that no air bubbles are present in the ultrasound coupling gel.
Establish the imaging wavelength(s) between 690 nm and 900 nm and the pulse repetition rate between 10 and 50 Hz.
Select the parameters for the acoustic data acquisition system – 1 MΩ input impedance.
Acquire 2030 samples for each laser pulse at a sampling rate of 40 megasamples per second and 12 bit vertical resolution.
Trigger the acquisition with Q-switch output of the laser.
Ensure that both the operator and the patient use protective goggles adapted to the optical excitation wavelength(s).
Set the laser power so that the light fluence at the tissue surface is maintained below 20 mJ/cm² during the experiment.
Start the pre-view software with a GPU implementation of processing algorithms.
Move the probe and/or the object to be imaged to optimize visualization performance.
Localize the structures of interest.
If necessary, inject a contrast agent prior to acquisition to enrich the contrast in the region of interest.
Start the hardware for data acquisition with the parameters described.
Gently move the probe around the imaged region to track the structures of interest.
Mount the imaged object and the hand-held probe onto the holder.
Start data acquisition with the parameters described, maintaining the execution of the pre-view software.
Maintain the optoacoustic probe and imaging part in the same position during the experiment.
Inject a contrast agent into the region of interest to track its dynamic distribution.
Stop the laser.
Remove the optoacoustic probe from the imaged region.
Stop the anesthesia supply for animal study.
Position the animal under an infrared heater to keep it warm.
Prevent the animal from contacting other animals until fully recovered from anesthesia.
Do not leave the animal unattended during recovery from anesthesia.
Load the file(s) containing acquired optoacoustic signals in the software application used for data processing.
Use a reconstruction algorithm to obtain a three-dimensional matrix array corresponding to a volumetric image of optical absorption for each frame and wavelength.
Use an unmixing algorithm to obtain, from each multi-wavelength frame, new sets of three-dimensional matrix arrays representing optical absorption for each absorbing substance present in the sample.
